standard_prerequisites.name: Description of an exceptional curve of the first kind
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the definition of an exceptional curve of the first kind as a curve isomorphic to a projective line whose normal sheaf pulls back to the twist by minus one
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the identification of the curve with a projective line and the computation of the cohomology of the twists by means of the normal sheaf.

standard_prerequisites.name: The ideal sheaf of a thickening and the associated short exact sequences
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard description of the ideal sheaf of the multiple nE of an effective Cartier divisor as the invertible sheaf of the negative multiple, giving the displayed short exact sequences
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the exact sequences comparing the sections over successive thickenings with the cohomology of the curve itself.

standard_prerequisites.name: Noetherianness and dimension of an adically complete local ring
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, the lemma that the completion of a Noetherian local ring is Noetherian and the proposition expressing the dimension through the growth of the powers of the maximal ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the Noetherianness and the dimension count for the limit ring.

core_obligations: Show the transition maps are surjective (proof lines 4616-4636): using the presentation of the curve as a projective line with normal sheaf the twist by minus one, the successive quotients in the displayed exact sequences have vanishing first cohomology, so the transition maps of the system of sections of the twists are surjective; for the untwisted case this gives an inverse system of surjections of rings with nilpotent kernels, hence the limit is a local ring with residue field the field of constants and with maximal ideal the limit of the kernels.

Identify the graded pieces (proof lines 4638-4654): choose two elements of the maximal ideal mapping to a basis of the twist by minus one, and observe that their monomials of degree d map to a basis of the corresponding space of sections of the twist by minus d on the curve; consequently the limit is separated and complete for the linear topology given by the kernels, the product of two such kernels sits in the next one, and the successive quotients are free over the field of constants on the monomials of the corresponding degree.

Conclude that the maximal ideal is generated by two elements (proof lines 4656-4672): expanding an element of one kernel along the monomial basis of the successive quotient shows by induction that every element of the d-th kernel is a combination of the two chosen elements with coefficients in the appropriate power, so the d-th kernel equals the d-th power of the ideal generated by them; hence the ring is complete for the topology of that ideal, Noetherian, of dimension two by the growth of the powers of the maximal ideal, and regular because its maximal ideal is generated by two elements.
proof_roadmap: Use the vanishing of the first cohomology of the relevant twists to make all transition maps surjective and to describe the maximal ideal of the limit.
Choose two generators and show that their monomials of each degree give bases of the successive quotients, so the limit is complete for the induced linear topology.
Expand elements along these monomial bases to identify the kernels with the powers of the ideal generated by the two chosen elements.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the limit of the sections of the structure sheaves of the thickenings of an exceptional curve of the first kind is a complete Noetherian regular local ring of dimension two, with the kernels of the comparison maps being the powers of its maximal ideal (statement lines 4603-4614). The proof (proof lines 4616-4675) uses the description of the curve as a projective line with normal sheaf the twist by minus one to obtain surjectivity of the transition maps, identifies the graded pieces through monomials in two chosen generators, and shows that the kernels are the powers of the ideal they generate. H3: an original computation with an explicit completion argument, written out in full.
